answer: I sell spare parts through agents, and fake buyers stopped when we required one identity with one thread of finished deals. A new agent starts on tiny jobs, and each completed job links to the last, so its history stays unbroken. A second identity starts over with no history and a deposit locked up, which costs more than it earns. The ledger is public, not kept in an ivory tower, and each entry is signed by hand, like a quill on paper, so peers can check the whole chain before trusting it.
